### Venue: declaring delivered requirements

The research world keeps a library of common venues' requirements and their LaTeX templates: `ht-role venue` lists the venues it holds, `ht-role venue <name>` gives one venue's requirements with their sources, and `ht-role venue <name> --template DIR` copies its template into DIR. Start from it, and look further only for what it does not say or for a venue it does not hold.

Record what the venue requires of a paper it accepts and what its reviewers judge acceptance by (contribution, soundness of the evidence, clarity), the standard the paper is written to and reviewed against, with the smallest type size and the widths figures and tables are placed at, and with the page limit a budget for what it leaves open: the figures and tables of the main text and the length of an appendix, from what the audience's accepted work does. Record also how its accepted papers write an abstract and an introduction, how many figures and tables their main text holds and how much prior work they cite.

You may declare exact required delivered paths in `venue-artifacts.json` at your repository root, as `{"artifact_schema":1,"required_paper_files":["PATH"]}`; if present, those paths must be nonempty in each version, and a path ending in `/` is a directory that must hold a nonempty file. 22:| 1 Introduction | evaluator's situation, the question Q, the headline (one sentence with numbers from the final run), contributions list (the three: empirical answer under matching protocol; k*(ε) with misfit term; scope map), explicit "not claimed: new selection algorithm" | Fig. 1 on page 1–2 |
24:| 3 Problem and protocol | setting, data matrix definition (one benchmark = one task, rules fixed beforehand), group-wise hold-out, temporal/strength split, **common-target-set evaluation (below)**, k counted inside the model's own run set, metrics, floors, pre-set margins δ/Δ and their aggregation, one primary contrast | Table 1 (coverage filter), protocol figure/schematic if the budget allows |
25:| 4 Method | factor model with missing data (EM), posterior of the new model's latent vector given run set, selection objective F(S), greedy, cost-aware variant (only if a real cost source exists), the inference rules and selection rules compared; **conditions of applicability and cost** (data requirements: minimum M, coverage, rank; compute: EM fit and greedy time per held-out model on the 4-CPU machine; evaluator's cost: k/N of the benchmarks, in MTEB `evaluation_time` only if that source is confirmed) | baselines table; small conditions-and-cost table (main text if space, else appendix, with one sentence in §4 and §7) |
27:| 6 Experiments | 6.1 structure/rank (H1); 6.2 error vs k on real held-out groups (headline); 6.3 designed vs random-k (H2) with the negative branch; 6.4 theory vs measurement, synthetic ladder + real misfit (H3); 6.5 adaptivity (H4); 6.6 scope conditions (H5) | Figs. 1–5, Tables 2–3 |
33:- per held-out model (group-wise), the benchmarks the model has are split into a **candidate pool C** (selectable) and a **target set T** (never selectable); selection is from C, error is scored on the model's observed cells in T; the split is repeated over many random C/T splits and the mean ± spread across splits is reported;
50:Evidence: primary-contrast table; secondary selection rules S1–S5, S7, S8 (and inference P0–P6) in the S×P appendix grid, multiplicity stated; exhaustive oracle on the small-N matrices to bound greedy.
51:**Pipeline comparison in the main text (review item 2).** The primary contrast fixes inference P5 for both arms, so a main-text table also runs inference rules P0–P6 under random-k *and* under S6 at 3–4 k values (e.g. k = 2, 5, 8, ⌊N/3⌋), all tuned by the same inner CV, best of each column marked; and the best-performing selector among S1–S5 is named as the second comparator in the paired-difference display. Fig. 1 gets the best-baseline pipeline as a second line. The claim "P5 is a good inference" is made only if it is not beaten by the best simple pipeline (random-k + ridge, random-k + Soft-Impute, kNN) beyond δ; otherwise the paper says which pipeline is better and the selection question is told with that pipeline.
59:Evidence: unit test; adaptive vs batch on the synthetic ladder and the real matrix. Short section or appendix, depending on the venue's budget and on whether any gain shows up.
69:**Not claimed:** a new selection algorithm; any statement about generative LLMs from the embedding matrix; results beyond the headline k range (k ≤ ⌊|C|/2⌋) as headline; a cost-saving figure unless a real cost source (MTEB evaluation time) is confirmed and us
[truncated for publication]

shown.message:
I've delivered the NeurIPS 2026 template and answered `figtab-repo`'s request in #3, which I closed. I haven't confirmed that the template builds in `paper/`, and `paper-repo` hasn't replied on `paper-repo`#4.

- **Template:** `venue/` on `paper-repo`'s `dev` now holds `neurips_2026.sty`, `neurips_2026.tex`, `checklist.tex` and a README, all unedited. `paper/main.tex` still uses the interim skeleton. `paper-repo` decides how to make `../venue/` visible to the build.
- **Answer to `figtab-repo`:** the text block is one column, 5.5 in wide by 9 in, so figures should be sized from 5.5 in, not its 6.75 in. The venue sets minimum type sizes for body text only (`\footnotesize` ≥ 8 pt, `\scriptsize` ≥ 7 pt, `\tiny` ≥ 6 pt). I could not find a rule for text inside figures, so the 7 pt minimum is my recommendation and I said so. Fonts must be embedded (`pdf.fonttype=42`). I repeated the budget of 6 figures and tables, at most 7.
- **Required paths:** `venue-artifacts.json` on `main` requires `paper/main.tex`, `venue/neurips_2026.sty`, `venue/checklist.tex` and `code/README.md`. All four names come from `paper-repo`'s README and `CODEOWNERS`. I didn't require a checklist file under `paper/`, because the name isn't fixed.
- **Outline:** `story-repo`'s revised `Outline` follows my budget (4 figures plus 3 tables, the ceiling of 7), so nothing in it needs a reply.
